learning_outcomes.text: To understand the theory and basic notions of technical drawing and its related standards
To know the main elements and modules of machines and mechanical systems
To draft technical drawings based on their application and the manufacturing processes needed to realize the parts
To compare design alternatives for mechanical systems based on external requirements
To develop adequate independence in the evaluation of mechanical systems for a correct design and representation
To develop a fluency in the representation of mechanical systems (both in hand-sketching and with the help of software tools)
To be able to provide new concepts and design solutions for components and assemblies considering the changing external requirements

syllabus_topics: Machine drawing basis: standards and standardization authorities
Isometric views: European system (first angle projection)
Designation and Relative Positions of Views
Sectional view types: Full Section, Half Section, Local Section
Dimensioning: definitions (dimension line, projection line, termination, value of the dimension)
Special indications for dimensioning (Diameters, Chords, Arcs, Angles, Radii, Chamfers, Tapered, etc.)
Arrangement of dimensions (chain dimensioning, parallel dimensioning, combined dimensioning, co-ordinate dimensioning)
Materials and technologies: chipping, grinding, milling, refining, etc.

Limits, Dimensional tolerances, and fits: Fundamental tolerances, Fundamental deviations, Method of placing limit dimensioning, Standards followed in industry (ISO), Fits (clearance, transition, interference)
Indicating Dimensional tolerances on the drawings
Indicating geometrical tolerances on the drawings
Indicating surface roughness on the drawings
Screw thread and Screwed fasteners: Introduction and nomenclature
Shaft couplings: keys, cotters, pins, and splined shafts
Bearings and seals: Introduction and classification
Seals (o-ring, v-ring, rotary shaft seal, etc.)
Introduction to parametric solid modeling (3D CAD)
PART environment - Navigation and visualization functions
Sketch definition in part design environment
DRAWING environment - Title block and views positioning
PART environment - Basic functions (extrusions, cuts, revolutions)
Specific basic features (chamfers, fillets, ribs, mirror, linear and circular patterns, shell)
DRAWING environment - View placement and dimensioning
PART environment - Advanced functions 2 (hole wizard, cosmetic threads, configurations)
DRAWING environment - Internal/external threads + drafted threads
ASSEMBLY environment - Basic functions (navigation, import, constraints, etc.)
DRAWING environment - Assembly drawing functions (bill of materials, balloon annotations, etc.)
ASSEMBLY environment - Advanced functions (importing standard components from libraries or public databases)
DRAWING environment - Functions and configuration management for assemblies
ASSEMBLY environment - Advanced functions (exploded views and assembly operation animations)
DRAWING environment - Functions and management of exploded views
Discussion on preparing a technical report and using Word/PPT
teaching_methods: Classroom lessons (50% lectures and 50% practical exercises/drawings) for Part A
Classroom lectures (50% lectures and 50% practical exercises using SolidWorks software) for Part B

assessment_methods.method: Writing assignment (overall assembly drawing, detailed drawing, technical questions) for Part A
CAD Project submission (complete 3D CAD models, 2D technical drawings, technical report) for Part B
Oral exam (PowerPoint Presentation, open-ended questions) for Part B

assessment_rules: For Part A, the exam consists of a written assignment (up to 3 hours) which includes a technical drawing of an assembly, a technical drawing of a component, and three technical questions. The grade is calculated considering the sum of results from both the drawing part and the technical questions. An optional oral exam, which can increase or decrease the grade (potentially resulting in failure), can be requested by emailing the teacher and is granted only after passing the written test. For Part B, the exam is a 1-hour oral exam, structured as a group project (maximum 3 students). Assessment includes the mandatory submission of a CAD Project (complete 3D CAD models, 2D technical drawings, technical report) one week before the oral exam. The oral exam consists of a 30-minute PowerPoint presentation and 30 minutes of open-ended questions focused on modeling strategies and SolidWorks functionality. Students must register for exams via the ESSE3 portal, and results are published on ESSE3 within one week of the exam date.
